learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Visual System.
Explain how the Visual System contributes to sensation, regulation or behaviour.
Connect Visual System function with clinically relevant symptoms.
Use lesion patterns and phenomenology cautiously rather than relying on one-to-one explanations.

anatomy.label: Retina
anatomy.detail: Photoreceptors and retinal circuits encode contrast, colour and timing.
anatomy.clinical: Retinal disease can mimic central visual dysfunction.

anatomy.label: Optic chiasm
anatomy.detail: Nasal retinal fibres cross to preserve contralateral hemifield mapping.
anatomy.clinical: Compression classically causes bitemporal field loss.

anatomy.label: Lateral geniculate nucleus
anatomy.clinical: Lesions can produce contralateral field deficits.

anatomy.label: Primary visual cortex
anatomy.detail: Represents edges, orientation and retinotopic position.
anatomy.clinical: Occipital lesions can cause homonymous field loss.

anatomy.label: Dorsal and ventral streams
anatomy.detail: Dorsal circuits guide action; ventral circuits support recognition.
anatomy.clinical: Damage can cause optic ataxia or visual agnosia.
